Rashi on Sukkah 41b:10:1.hebrew: הוה מצלי ביה - כשהיה מתפלל, היה לולבו בידו. מרוב חיבתו עליו, היה מתפלל בו:
Rashi on Sukkah 41b:10:1.english: He would pray with it - When he would pray, his lulav was in his hand. Out of his great love for it, he would pray with it.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:10:2.hebrew: לא יאחז אדם כו' ויתפלל - מפני שטרוד הוא במחשבתו שלא יפלו מידו ויתבזו, ואין דעתו מיושבת עליו בתפלתו:
Rashi on Sukkah 41b:10:2.english: A person should not hold, etc., and pray - Because he is preoccupied in his thoughts lest they fall from his hand and be disgraced, and his mind is not settled during his prayer.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:10:3.hebrew: לא יישן בהם לא שינת קבע ולא שינת עראי - שמא יפלו מידו. והכי אוקימנא ליה בהישן (לעיל סוכה דף כו.), דהא דקתני "לא קבע ולא עראי" — בדנקיט ליה בידיה:
Rashi on Sukkah 41b:10:3.english: Nor should he sleep with them, neither a deep sleep nor a brief nap - Lest they fall from his hand. And thus we established it in [the chapter] Hayashen (above, Sukkah 26a): that that which was taught, “neither regular nor temporary [sleep],” [is] when he is holding them in his hand.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:11:1.english: A knife - He is afraid lest it fall and stick into his foot.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:11:4.english: And a loaf - For if it falls, it will become repulsive.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:11:5.hebrew: לאו מצוה נינהו - לאוחזן, והויין עליו למשא. לפיכך, טרוד במשאם, וכבד עליו משאם ושמירתם:
Rashi on Sukkah 41b:11:5.english: They are not a mitzvah - [It is not a mitzvah] to hold them, and they become a burden upon him. Therefore, he is preoccupied with their burden, and their burden and their safeguarding weigh heavily upon him.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:11:6.hebrew: הכא - נטילתה ולקיחתה מצוה היא, ומתוך שחביבה מצוה עליו, אין משאה ושימורה כבד עליו, ולא טריד:
Rashi on Sukkah 41b:11:6.english: Here - Taking it and holding it is a mitzvah; and since the mitzvah is beloved to him, carrying it and guarding it are not burdensome upon him, and he is not preoccupied.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:12:1.hebrew: קורא בתורה - צריך להניח הלולב, לפי שגולל ס"ת ופותחו:
Rashi on Sukkah 41b:12:1.english: He reads from the Torah - He must set down the lulav, because he rolls the Torah scroll and opens it.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:12:2.english: He enters the study hall - He is preoccupied with the study, and [the lulav] will fall from his hands.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:1:1.english: “Until [this] selfsame [day]” — until the essence of the day - The entire day is called “the essence of the day.”

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:1:2.hebrew: וקסבר עד ועד בכלל - ולא דריש: "עד" — ולא עד בכלל, להתירו בהאיר מזרח כי ליכא עומר. והכי מתוקמא קראי: אין עומר — "עד עצם", ועד בכלל; יש עומר — "עד הביאכם":
Rashi on Sukkah 41b:1:2.english: And he holds [that] "until" [means] "until" is inclusive - And he does not expound [that] "until" [means] "until" is not inclusive, so as to permit it at the illuminating of the eastern sky when there is no omer. And this is how the verses are established: [When there is] no omer — "until this selfsame [day]," and "until" is inclusive; [when there] is an omer — "until you bring [the offering of your God]."

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:2:1.hebrew: והא מיפלג פליג - רבי יהודה עליה, שמצינו שתמה רבי יהודה בדורו על תקנת ריב"ז: למה תלה הדבר בעצמו — דמשמע לעשות סייג בא — והלא מן התורה הוא אסור:
Rashi on Sukkah 41b:2:1.english: But doesn't he disagree - Rabbi Yehuda [disagrees] with him, for we find that Rabbi Yehuda in his generation wondered at the ordinance of Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai: Why did he attribute the matter to himself — which implies that he came to make a [rabbinic] fence — when isn't it forbidden by Torah law?

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:3:1.english: He expounded - The verse: “Until” — and “until” is inclusive.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:3:2.hebrew: והתקין - לפי שהיו רגילים לאכול חדש מחצות ולהלן כשהיה הבית קיים, עד עכשיו — הוצרך לתקן:
Rashi on Sukkah 41b:3:2.english: And he instituted - Because they were accustomed to eat new grain from midday onward when the Temple stood, until now — he needed to institute an ordinance.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:4:1.hebrew: י"ט הראשון כו' - דאמרינן לקמן (סוכה דף מג.), דדוחה מצות לולב שבת בי"ט הראשון לבדו:
Rashi on Sukkah 41b:4:1.english: The first Festival day, etc. - For we say below (Sukkah 43a) that the mitzvah of the lulav overrides Shabbat on the first Festival day alone.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:4:2.english: Bring their lulavim - On the eve of Shabbat.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:4:3.hebrew: שהוציאו ברשות - ברשות מצוה, שהיה טרוד במצוה, ומחשב ועסוק וממהר לעשותה, ומתוך כך טעה ושכח שהוא שבת. וקסבר רבי יוסי: טעה בדבר מצוה ושגג בדבר כרת — פטור מקרבן:
Rashi on Sukkah 41b:4:3.english: [Because] he carried it out with permission - With the authorization of a mitzvah; for he was preoccupied with the mitzvah, and thinking [about it], occupied, and rushing to perform it, and as a result of this he erred and forgot that it was Shabbat. And Rabbi Yosei maintains: [One who] erred in a matter of a mitzvah and committed an unwitting transgression in a matter [punishable by] excision is exempt from a sacrifice.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:5:1.english: From where are these matters - That a person does not fulfill [his obligation] with the lulav of his fellow.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:5:2.english: “For yourselves” [means] from your own - It implies [this].

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:7:1.hebrew: למה לי למימר החזירו - מה אנו למידין מחזרה זו, דאצטריך תנא למיתנייה במתני':
Rashi on Sukkah 41b:7:1.english: Why do I need to say: “He returned it”? - What do we learn from this return, that the Tanna needed to teach it in the Mishnah?

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:7:2.hebrew: הא קמ"ל - דר"ג ע"מ שיחזירוהו לו נתנו להם, ואפ"ה הויא מתנה, עד שיצאו בו:
Rashi on Sukkah 41b:7:2.english: This teaches us - That Rabban Gamliel gave it to them on condition that they return it to him, and even so it is [considered] a gift, so that they fulfilled their obligation with it.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:8:1.hebrew: החזירו לו יצא - דמתנה על מנת להחזיר מתנה היא, והרי החזירו לו. אבל אם לא החזירו, אגלאי מלתא דמעיקרא גזול הוא בידו:
Rashi on Sukkah 41b:8:1.english: [If] he returned it to him, he fulfilled [his obligation] - For a gift [given] on condition that [he] return it is a [valid] gift, and behold, he returned it to him. But if he did not return it, it is revealed that from the outset it was stolen in his possession.

Rashi on Sukkah 41b:9:1.hebrew: ה"ג למה ליה למימר שלקחו באלף זוז - להודיעך כמה מצות חביבות עליהם:
Rashi on Sukkah 41b:9:1.english: This is the reading: Why did he have to say that he bought it for a thousand zuz? - To inform you how beloved mitzvot were to them.

Tosafot on Sukkah 41b:11:1.hebrew: ואמר שמואל סכין וקערה וככר ומעות הרי אלו כיוצא בהן - אצטריך ליה לשמואל למימר, דלא תימא: דווקא תפילין וס"ת, דאיכא בזיון כתבי הקודש בנפילתו, טריד בהו טפי, ואין דעתו מתיישבת בתפלתו:
Tosafot on Sukkah 41b:11:1.english: And Shmuel said: A knife, a bowl, a loaf, and money — these are like them - It was necessary for Shmuel to say [this], so that you should not say: Specifically [regarding] tefillin and a Torah scroll, where there is degradation of the sacred writings if it falls, is he especially preoccupied with them and his mind is not settled during his prayer.

Tosafot on Sukkah 41b:5:1.hebrew: ולקחתם שתהא לקיחה לכל א' וא' - מדלא כתיב ״ולקחת״ לשון יחיד. וגבי סוכה לא צריך קרא, דהא כתיב: ״כל האזרח״:
Tosafot on Sukkah 41b:5:1.english: “And you shall take,” that there should be taking for each and every one - [This is derived] from the fact that it is not written “And you shall take” in the singular form. And regarding sukkah, a verse is not needed, as it is written: “All the native-born” [Leviticus 23:42].

Tosafot on Sukkah 41b:5:2.hebrew: אלא א"כ נתן לו במתנה - ובאתרוג השותפין נמי לא נפיק, כדמוכח בשילהי יש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קלז: ושם) גבי אחין שקנו אתרוג בתפיסת הבית, ולא חשיב שלו כיון דאין מיוחד שלו, אלא כשאול הוי ואינו יוצא בו. ומה שנהגו הקהל לקנות אתרוג בשותפות — מלמדין אותן שיהו כולם נותן כל אחד ואחד חלקו לחבירו על מנת להחזיר. ויש לסמוך, דכיון דקנאוהו על מנת לצאת בו, ואע"ג שלא פירשו — סתמא דמלתא כאילו פרשו דמי, כיון דבענין אחר אין יכולין לצאת בו:
Tosafot on Sukkah 41b:5:2.english: "Unless he gave it to him as a gift" - And with a jointly owned etrog as well, one does not fulfill [his obligation], as is proven at the end of [the chapter entitled] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 137b, and see there) regarding brothers who bought an etrog from the undivided estate, and it is not considered his, since it is not designated as his; rather, it is [treated] like a borrowed [etrog], and he does not fulfill [his obligation] with it. And as for that which the community is accustomed to purchase an etrog in partnership — we instruct them that all of them, each and every one, should give his share to his fellow [as a gift] on condition that it be returned. And one can rely [on the principle] that since they purchased it in order to fulfill [their obligation] with it, even though they did not explicitly specify [this transfer], the default assumption is considered as though they had specified it, since in any other manner they cannot fulfill [their obligation] with it.

Tosafot on Sukkah 41b:8:1.hebrew: הילך אתרוג זה במתנה על מנת שתחזירהו לי - בשום מקום אין מדקדק הש"ס בלשונו להקדים תנאי למעשה, ותנאי כפול, והן קודם ללאו, אע"ג דבהכי מיירי; אלא שמקצר לשונו, לפי שלא על חידוש זה בא להשמיענו. ולא דמי לתנאי ומעשה בדבר אחד, דהיינו כששניהם סותרים זה את זה, כי ההיא ד"על מנת שתחזיר לי את הנייר" בפרק מי שאחזו (גיטין דף עה. ושם). וא"ת: כיון דאמר ע"מ שתחזירו לי, א"כ אם הקדישו אינו מקודש, כדמוכח בסוף יש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קלז:) גבי "שור זה נתון לך במתנה ע"מ שתחזירהו לי", דכיון דקאמר "לי" — מידי דחזי לי קאמר; וא"כ היאך יצא? והא אנן תנן בנדרים פרק השותפין (נדרים דף מח.) גבי מתנה דבית חורון, דכל מתנה שאינה שאם הקדישה לא תהא מקודשת — לא שמיה מתנה! וי"ל: דה"נ הוי בידו להקדיש, להיות קדוש כל זמן שהוא בידו עד שיחזיר. ועוד, דהתם נמי לא בהקדש תלוי טעם המתנה, כדמוכח בנדרים ירושלמי, דאמר עלה רבי ירמיה: רבי יהודה בעי, מעתה מתנה — אין אדם נותן מתנה לחבירו ע"מ שלא יקדשנה לשמים?! ומשני: מתני' — כל מתנה שהיא כמתנת בית חורון, שהיתה בערמה, שאם הקדישה אינה מוקדשת — אינה מתנה; כלומר, שלא נתנה לו שיהנה המקבל שום הנאה שבעולם, אלא שיהא מותר לאביו של נותן, זה ודאי הערמה בעלמא ולא שמיה מתנה, שהרי לא זכה בה לענין עצמו לשום דבר, וא"כ מה הקנה לו? אבל הכא דמזכה ליה שיהנה בו — שמיה מתנה. ולא הזכיר שם הקדש אלא משום שעל הקדש היה מעשה. ולשון "כל מתנה שאינה וכו'" מוכיח כן, דמשמע שאינה מתנה לשום דבר. גם סעודתו היתה מוכחת עליו שלא היה דעתו ליתן כלל לענין שום דבר, רק שיבא אביו ויאכל, כמו שמפרש שם בגמרא; או משום דויתור אסור במודר הנאה. אבל בעלמא מתנה היא, אע"פ שאין יכול להקדישה, כדתנן פרק בתרא דנדרים (דף פח.) שנותן לבתו מה שנושאת ונותנת לפיה, ובפ"ק דקדושין (דף כג: ושם) שנותן לעבד ע"מ שיצא בו לחירות:
Tosafot on Sukkah 41b:8:1.english: "Here is this etrog for you as a gift on condition that you return it to me" - Nowhere is the Shas exacting in its phrasing to place the condition before the act, [or to formulate] a double condition, or [to place] the affirmative before the negative, even though it is dealing with such [requirements]; rather, it abbreviates its phrasing because it did not come to teach us about this novel legal rule. And this is not similar to a condition and an act in a single matter, that is, when the two contradict one another, such as that [case] of "on condition that you return the paper to me" in the chapter [entitled] Mi She'achazo (Gittin 75a and there). And if you should say: Since he said, "on condition that you return it to me," if so, if he consecrated it, it is not consecrated, as is proved at the end of [the chapter entitled] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 137b) regarding "This ox is given to you as a gift on condition that you return it to me" — for since he said "to me," he meant something that is fit for me [to use]; and if so, how did he fulfill his obligation [with the etrog]? For didn't we learn in the Mishnah in Nedarim, in the chapter [entitled] HaShutafin (Nedarim 48a), regarding the gift of Beit Choron, that "any gift that is not [such] that if he consecrated it, it would be consecrated, is not called a gift"? And one can say: Here too, it was within his power to consecrate [it], to be consecrated for the entire time that it is in his possession until he returns [it]. And furthermore, there too the reason [it is not] a gift is not dependent on consecration, as is proved in Nedarim in the Yerushalmi, which states regarding it: Rabbi Yirmeyah [said], Rabbi Yehudah asked: "From now [on, regarding] a gift, may a person not give a gift to his fellow on condition that he not consecrate it to Heaven?!" And it answers: The Mishnah [means]: "Any gift that is like the gift of Beit Choron, which was [done] with deceit, such that if he consecrated it, it is not consecrated, is not a gift" — that is to say, since he did not give it to him for the recipient to derive any benefit in the world [from it], but rather only that it should be permitted to this giver's father, this is certainly a mere evasion and is not called a gift, for he did not acquire it for himself for any purpose, and if so, what did he transfer to him? But here, where he transfers ownership to him so that he may benefit from it, it is called a gift. And it mentioned consecration there only because the incident involved consecration. And the wording "any gift that is not, etc." proves this, as it implies that it is not a gift for any purpose. Also, his banquet proved about him that it was not his intention to give [it] at all for any purpose, except only that his father should come and eat, as [the Gemara] explains there in the Gemara; or because indulgence [vitur] is forbidden to one who is prohibited from deriving benefit. However, generally speaking, it is a gift even though he cannot consecrate it, as we learned in the Mishnah in the final chapter of Nedarim (88a): where one gives to his daughter whatever she buys and sells for her food; and in the first chapter of Kiddushin (23b and there): where one gives [funds] to a slave on condition that he go free with it.

Tosafot on Sukkah 41b:8:2.hebrew: ואם לאו לא יצא - ומה שלא החזירו רבי יהושע לרבן גמליאל, אלא נתנו לרבי אלעזר בן עזריה, ורבי אלעזר בן עזריה לרבי עקיבא — דעתו של רבן גמליאל היה שיצאו כולם, ואח"כ יחזירוהו:
Tosafot on Sukkah 41b:8:2.english: "And if not, he did not fulfill [his obligation]" - And as for that which Rabbi Yehoshua did not return it to Rabban Gamliel, but rather gave it to Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah, and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah [gave it] to Rabbi Akiva — Rabban Gamliel's intention was that they should all fulfill [their obligation], and afterward they would return it.
